import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns
import numpy as np

# Load data
df = pd.read_csv('data/cameras.csv')

# Create a comprehensive multi-panel visualization
fig = plt.figure(figsize=(16, 10))
gs = fig.add_gridspec(3, 3, hspace=0.3, wspace=0.3)

# 1. Price distribution by sensor type
ax1 = fig.add_subplot(gs[0, :2])
sensor_order = df.groupby('sensor_type')['price_usd'].median().sort_values(ascending=False).index
sns.boxplot(data=df, x='sensor_type', y='price_usd', order=sensor_order, ax=ax1, palette='Set2')
ax1.set_title('Price Distribution by Sensor Type', fontsize=14, fontweight='bold')
ax1.set_xlabel('Sensor Type', fontsize=11)
ax1.set_ylabel('Price (USD)', fontsize=11)
ax1.tick_params(axis='x', rotation=45)

# 2. Megapixels vs Price colored by sensor type
ax2 = fig.add_subplot(gs[0, 2])
for sensor in df['sensor_type'].unique():
    sensor_data = df[df['sensor_type'] == sensor]
    ax2.scatter(sensor_data['megapixels'], sensor_data['price_usd'], 
               alpha=0.6, s=30, label=sensor)
ax2.set_title('Megapixels vs Price', fontsize=12, fontweight='bold')
ax2.set_xlabel('Megapixels', fontsize=10)
ax2.set_ylabel('Price (USD)', fontsize=10)
ax2.legend(fontsize=8, loc='upper left')

# 3. Camera evolution over time
ax3 = fig.add_subplot(gs[1, :])
year_stats = df.groupby('model_year').agg({
    'megapixels': 'mean',
    'max_iso': 'mean',
    'price_usd': 'mean'
}).reset_index()

ax3_twin1 = ax3.twinx()
ax3_twin2 = ax3.twinx()
ax3_twin2.spines['right'].set_position(('outward', 60))

p1 = ax3.plot(year_stats['model_year'], year_stats['megapixels'], 
             marker='o', linewidth=2, color='#2E86AB', label='Avg Megapixels')
p2 = ax3_twin1.plot(year_stats['model_year'], year_stats['max_iso'], 
                   marker='s', linewidth=2, color='#A23B72', label='Avg Max ISO')
p3 = ax3_twin2.plot(year_stats['model_year'], year_stats['price_usd'], 
                   marker='^', linewidth=2, color='#F18F01', label='Avg Price')

ax3.set_xlabel('Model Year', fontsize=11)
ax3.set_ylabel('Megapixels', fontsize=11, color='#2E86AB')
ax3_twin1.set_ylabel('Max ISO', fontsize=11, color='#A23B72')
ax3_twin2.set_ylabel('Price (USD)', fontsize=11, color='#F18F01')
ax3.tick_params(axis='y', labelcolor='#2E86AB')
ax3_twin1.tick_params(axis='y', labelcolor='#A23B72')
ax3_twin2.tick_params(axis='y', labelcolor='#F18F01')
ax3.set_title('Camera Technology Evolution Over Time', fontsize=14, fontweight='bold')
ax3.grid(True, alpha=0.3)

# 4. 4K video capability by body type
ax4 = fig.add_subplot(gs[2, 0])
video_4k_by_body = df.groupby('body_type')['has_video_4k'].agg(['sum', 'count'])
video_4k_by_body['percentage'] = (video_4k_by_body['sum'] / video_4k_by_body['count'] * 100)
video_4k_sorted = video_4k_by_body.sort_values('percentage', ascending=True)
ax4.barh(video_4k_sorted.index, video_4k_sorted['percentage'], color='#06A77D')
ax4.set_xlabel('% with 4K Video', fontsize=10)
ax4.set_ylabel('Body Type', fontsize=10)
ax4.set_title('4K Video Support by Body Type', fontsize=12, fontweight='bold')
ax4.grid(axis='x', alpha=0.3)

# 5. Weight vs Price by body type
ax5 = fig.add_subplot(gs[2, 1])
body_types = df['body_type'].value_counts().head(4).index
colors = sns.color_palette('husl', len(body_types))
for i, body in enumerate(body_types):
    body_data = df[df['body_type'] == body]
    ax5.scatter(body_data['weight_grams'], body_data['price_usd'], 
               alpha=0.5, s=40, label=body, color=colors[i])
ax5.set_xlabel('Weight (grams)', fontsize=10)
ax5.set_ylabel('Price (USD)', fontsize=10)
ax5.set_title('Weight vs Price by Body Type', fontsize=12, fontweight='bold')
ax5.legend(fontsize=9)

# 6. Brand distribution (top 10)
ax6 = fig.add_subplot(gs[2, 2])
top_brands = df['brand'].value_counts().head(10)
ax6.pie(top_brands.values, labels=top_brands.index, autopct='%1.1f%%', 
       startangle=90, textprops={'fontsize': 8})
ax6.set_title('Top 10 Brands Distribution', fontsize=12, fontweight='bold')

plt.suptitle('Digital Camera Market Analysis Dashboard', 
            fontsize=16, fontweight='bold', y=0.995)

plt.savefig('output.png', bbox_inches='tight', dpi=150)
